heroHeadline: FIFA Leadership Crisis Deepens: Nordic Federations Revolt, Čeferin Says Infantino Must Quit or Face a Challenger
heroSubtitle: A month after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time to win the World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium (July 19), the tournament's aftermath has been overtaken by a FIFA governance crisis. Infantino's abandoned plan to sell a 20% stake in a new World Cup commercial entity to private investors triggered a widening federation revolt through August — Ireland, New Zealand, Scotland, Israel, Montenegro, and North Macedonia all withdrew re-election support, and FIFA fired COO Kevin Lamour (Aug 17) after he accused Infantino of misleading staff. The crisis escalated over the weekend: Infantino defied a CONCACAF request and attended a Caribbean Football Union event in the Dominican Republic (Aug 22), widely read as lobbying for re-election votes; all six Nordic federations declared they had 'lost confidence' in him and demanded an independent investigation (Aug 23); and UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin ruled out a rival bid of his own but said Infantino must either step down or 'have a candidate against him' at the March 18, 2027 election in Rabat, naming AFC president Sheikh Salman and CONCACAF's Victor Montagliani as possible challengers (Aug 24). Separately, FIFA's Disciplinary Committee banned three Argentina players, including a 10-match suspension for Leandro Paredes, over the post-final scuffle with Spain (Aug 21).
